title: Japanese greetings and writing
examples: What is the difference between hiragana and katakana?
How do I start learning kanji?

explain.say: Today we say konnichiwa. It is a very common Japanese greeting.

items: It means hello or good afternoon.
It is used in many daily situations.

explain.say: Next we learn about hiragana. Hiragana is one of the Japanese writing systems.
Then we look at katakana. Katakana is the second Japanese writing system we study.
Finally, we learn about kanji. Kanji are characters adopted from Chinese writing.
When you write your name, you might use all three scripts. You might write your name using hiragana and kanji.
A real life example is reading a Japanese menu. You will see kanji for food names and hiragana for grammar.

faq.q: What is the main difference between the three scripts?
faq.a: Hiragana is for native Japanese words. Katakana is mostly for foreign words. Kanji carry the main meaning.
asks: Which script is easiest to learn?
Do I learn them in order?

faq.q: Do I need to know all the characters at once?
faq.a: No, you learn them gradually. You start with basic greetings and simple words first.
asks: Is there a better order to learn?

faq.a: It is a general greeting used during the day. It is similar to saying 'good day' in English.
asks: Is konnichiwa only for the afternoon?
What is the formal way to say hello?

faq.q: Can kanji be used for simple words?
faq.a: Kanji are best for concepts and nouns. Hiragana is better for grammar and particles.
asks: Does every word have a kanji?

faq.q: If I see a mix of scripts, what should I read first?
faq.a: Look for the kanji first to get the main idea. Then use hiragana to read the flow around it.
asks: How do I read mixed text?
Which script is the most important?

facts: Konnichiwa means hello or good afternoon.
Hiragana is used for native Japanese words and grammar.
Katakana is often used for words from other languages.
Kanji characters represent ideas or concepts.

quiz.say: Which script is primarily used for native Japanese words and grammar particles?
quiz.why: Hiragana is the basic phonetic script for native Japanese words.

wrong.0: Konnichiwa is a greeting, not a writing system itself.
wrong.2: Kanji are characters that represent ideas or concepts, not just sounds.
wrong.3: Katakana is mainly reserved for words borrowed from foreign languages.

quiz.say: If you see the word for 'computer' written in Japanese, which script is it most likely to use?
quiz.why: Because 'computer' is a foreign loanword, katakana is the standard choice.

wrong.0: Hiragana is usually for words that come naturally in Japanese.
wrong.1: Kanji might be used, but katakana is more common for loanwords.
wrong.2: Konnichiwa is a greeting, not a script type.

quiz.say: When writing a simple sentence like 'I eat rice,' which script combination would you most likely see?
quiz.why: The main noun (rice) uses kanji, and the grammar words (I, eat) use hiragana.

wrong.1: Katakana is not used for basic sentence structure.
wrong.2: Kanji alone cannot show the small grammar particles needed.
wrong.3: Konnichiwa is only for greetings, not full sentences.
